title: Moving math into methods
summary: DriveMath: numbers in, a number out.

say.never: A **method** is a named job. This one is called `toFahrenheit`. You hand it a number, it does a little math, and it hands back one answer. `return` is how it hands the answer back.
say.bit: A method takes inputs, computes, and returns one result.

say.never: This is `rotationsToMeters`, already in your file. You hand it two numbers and it hands back one answer. The first line is its **signature**: its name and what it takes.
say.bit: `rotationsToMeters` takes two numbers and returns one. The first line is its signature.

say.never: Keeping math in its own methods means each one never touches a motor or sensor, so you can test it on its own with plain numbers. The code that uses it then reads almost like a sentence: "give me the temperature in Fahrenheit". If the math has a bug, you know exactly which method to fix.
say.bit: Pure math methods are easy to test and make the calling code read like a sentence.

say.never: These math methods live in a file called `DriveMath` and never touch a motor. That makes each one easy to check on its own, and it makes the robot code read almost like English: "give me the linear speed".
say.bit: `DriveMath` never touches a motor or sensor, so each method can be tested on its own. The drivetrain calls them, and `Robot.java` reads almost like a sentence.

say.never: A signature has four parts, in this order: `public static`, the type of the answer, the name, and then the inputs in parentheses, each with its type. The name must match exactly, capital letters and all, because the robot code calls it by that name. Here the answer and every input are `double`.
say.bit: Signature: `public static`, answer type, name, then (type and name for each input). Match the name exactly.

say.never: Under the comment, write `linearSpeed` yourself. Inputs: the left speed and the right speed, both `double`. Answer: a `double`, the average of the two sides. Call the inputs `left_meters_per_second` and `right_meters_per_second`. Save, then press **Verify**.
say.bit: Write `linearSpeed(left, right)`: two doubles in, the average out. Then **Verify**.

say.bit: Write `angularSpeed(left, right, track_width_meters)`: three doubles in, `(right - left) / track_width_meters` out.
